named_cards: Attempt on An iid FPP law with proved KPZ exponent relation

Chatterjee (2013) proved the KPZ scaling relation chi = 2 xi - 1 for first-passage percolation on Z^d - but ONLY for his own strengthened definitions of the exponents, ONLY under the assumption that those strengthened exponents exist, and ONLY for 'nearly Gamma' weight laws. The Auffinger-Damron-Hanson survey records that Chatterjee's exponents are not known to exist for ANY distribution of passage times, so as of the survey the relation is established for no distribution at all, and proving it remains open.
Open problem: An iid FPP law with proved KPZ exponent relation

Auffinger-Damron (2014) reprove only ONE of the two inequalities in the first-passage percolation scaling relation - they obtain chi <= 2 xi - 1, still assuming that the exponents defined in Chatterjee (2013) exist, but WITHOUT Chatterjee's 'nearly Gamma' assumption. So the nearly-Gamma hypothesis is removable for the '<=' direction and, as of the survey, not for the equality.
